newsitem.title: FRANCE: Tentative agreement in Franco-British fishing row.
newsitem.headline: Tentative agreement in Franco-British fishing row.

text.p: French and British diplomats reached tentative agreement on Thursday about resolving a dispute over the rights of French fishermen to work near the British Channel island of Guernsey off the Normandy coast.
A joint communique said British representatives presented a draft accord which took into account French demands.

Asserting that fishing the was vital for seaside inhabitants of both countries, it said the two countries agreed a commission made up of officials from both countries and representatives of the fishing industry could advise on administration of fishing grounds.
The two sides agreed a zone could be set aside where licensed fishermen from both countries would have guaranteed fishing rights, taking into account preservation of resources, the statement said.
The two sides agreed to meet again in London on June 9 to pursue study of a new fishing regime for the area, it said.
The dispute was triggered when Britain unilaterally withdrew from a 1994 agreement granting fishing rights to France in the zone.

French sources said at the time that authorities on the British island of Guernsey had gone back on a two-year-old arrangement which allowed French trawlers to operate in the island's waters in return for rights for Guernsey fishermen to fish in French waters.
